tools.name: query_database
tools.description:
⭐ PRIMARY TOOL - Use this FIRST for any SOJO-specific question.

This tool uses intelligent RAG retrieval to find SQL patterns, documentation, and domain knowledge. It handles production data, equipment specs, machine capabilities, and company-specific information.

⚠️ PRODUCTION vs MACHINE DATA:
- Production totals ("how many did we produce?") → Assembly Build views (NetSuite)
- Efficiency/uptime/downtime/OEE → Raven (machine data)
- If user explicitly says "Raven" for production → use Raven
- DEFAULT: production quantity = Assembly Build, machine metrics = Raven

🚨 ALWAYS query this tool for SOJO-specific information - do NOT answer from general knowledge.

ALWAYS START HERE - Do NOT use list_tables, describe_table, or validate_sku_line_feasibility first.

🚨 CRITICAL: Copy the user's question CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER as a literal string.
- Do NOT rephrase, expand, clarify, or "improve" the wording
- Do NOT add words like "production", "manufacturing", "facility", "currently"
- Do NOT fix grammar or capitalization
- The tool uses semantic matching that REQUIRES the user's exact phrasing
- Any modification will break template matching and cause failures

SCHEDULING QUERIES - Built-in validation:
- Pass the COMPLETE request: "Schedule VP28103 (7200 cases), VP28104 (5000 cases) on BS1, Monday 7am, maximize margin"
- The tool automatically validates SKU compatibility
- If validation fails, it returns issues WITH your original request preserved
- After user clarifies, re-call with the CORRECTED complete request
- Do NOT call validate_sku_line_feasibility directly - this tool handles it

The tool automatically retrieves:
- SQL templates for common query patterns
- Schema information for correct column names
- Domain knowledge FAQs for context

This tool supports THREE modes:

MODE 1: Natural Language Question (PREFERRED)
- Provide 'question' parameter with your question in plain English
- Example: question="What is my most profitable SKU?"
- Example: question="Build schedule for VP28103 (7200 cases), VP28104 (5000) on ID1, Monday 7am, maximize margin"

SOP / VP LOOKUP QUERIES — ALWAYS use this tool for ANY question about a VP code or SOP:
- "Show me all SOPs for VP13030" → returns all SOP records for that SKU
- "Compare SOPs for VP13030" → returns all versions/lines to compare
- "What are the differences between VP13030 SOPs?" → use this, NOT memory/chat search
- "How many people to run Refresco Bloom 3-flv 18pk?" → staffing from SOP data
- "What SOPs were created yesterday?" → recently created SOPs
- ANY mention of "VP" + digits = use this tool with skus hint

MODE 2: Direct SQL (Only if you have specific SQL from a previous response)
- Provide 'query' parameter with SQL
- TABLE SCHEMAS: NS_MAIN is in SYSTEMS_DATA.SILVER (margins/pricing/CPM). ITEM_SOP_RECORD is in SYSTEMS_DATA.SILVER (SOP operational data). PLANNING_FORMAT is in SYSTEMS_DATA.SILVER. CHANGEOVERS, LINE_SPECS are in SYSTEMS_DATA.METADATA. RAVEN_SEGMENTS is in MACHINEDATA.PUBLIC.

MODE 3: Knowledge/Culture Questions
- Example: question="What is the SOJO MOJO?"

For DIELINE ANALYSIS, use the analyze_dieline tool instead.

The response includes the SQL pattern used - reuse it for follow-up queries.

OPTIONAL ENTITY HINTS (improve accuracy when provided):
- skus: VP codes from the question (e.g., ["VP103003", "VP59024"])
- line: Line or machine name (e.g., "BS1", "CTC40")
- num_flavors: Flavor count from "4 flv", "4-flavor" → 4
- pack_size: Pack size from "12pk", "12-pack", "24PK" → 12
- difference_type: Changeover type (e.g., "format_type", "container")
- desc1, desc2: Product descriptions for changeover
- output_case: Inner case count from NxM patterns like "3x8" → 8, "4x6" → 6 (the M, not total)
When present, these skip internal regex extraction. When absent, extraction is automatic.
Only fill these when the user's message clearly contains the information.

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description:
List available tables in a database schema.

⚠️ PREFER query_database FIRST - It has built-in knowledge of table structures and optimized SQL patterns. Only use list_tables if query_database doesn't have the information you need.

Databases:
- planning (default): SYSTEMS_DATA.METADATA (changeovers, line specs) + SYSTEMS_DATA.SILVER (PLANNING_FORMAT, NS_MAIN pricing/margins) + SYSTEMS_DATA.SILVER (ITEM_SOP_RECORD SOP data)
- machine: MACHINEDATA.PUBLIC - Raven machine metrics (efficiency, uptime, downtime, OEE — NOT production totals)

tools.name: describe_table
tools.description:
Get table schema (columns, data types).

⚠️ PREFER query_database FIRST - It has built-in knowledge of table schemas and optimized SQL patterns for common queries (profitability, changeovers, efficiency). Only use describe_table if you need raw column details not available through query_database.

Key tables (with schema):
- ITEM_SOP_RECORD (SYSTEMS_DATA.SILVER): SOP operational data (headcount, pallets, lot codes, labels)
- NS_MAIN (SYSTEMS_DATA.SILVER): SKU pricing, margins, CPM rates
- PLANNING_FORMAT (SYSTEMS_DATA.SILVER): Product specifications (SKU attributes)
- RAVEN_SEGMENTS (MACHINEDATA.PUBLIC): Machine metrics — efficiency, uptime, downtime, OEE (NOT production totals)
- LINE_SPECS (SYSTEMS_DATA.METADATA): Changeover rules + format compatibility (PACKAGING_TYPES) ONLY. Line inventory, machine identity/type, and facility come from MASTER_ASSET (OEM/MODEL_NAME/ASSET_TYPE/WAREHOUSE) + MASTER_BAY_ASSIGNMENT, NOT LINE_SPECS.
- CHANGEOVERS (SYSTEMS_DATA.METADATA): Changeover time rules

tools.name: get_table_sample
tools.description:
Get sample rows from a table.

⚠️ PREFER query_database FIRST - It has optimized SQL patterns that already know the correct columns and joins. Only use get_table_sample for edge cases where you need to see raw data not covered by query_database.

Returns first N rows (default: 5).

tools.name: analyze_dieline
tools.description:
ALWAYS use this tool when a user uploads or shares a carton, dieline, packaging
blueprint, or box drawing image — even if they just ask "what are the dimensions?"
Do NOT try to read dimensions from the image yourself — this tool has reference
guides and CLIP matching that produce far more accurate results.

Also use this tool for: "carton dimensions", "case dimensions", "flap dimensions",
"can this carton run on [line]", "dieline compatibility", "analyze this dieline".

A dieline is a blueprint for packaging — it maps out cut lines, creases, perforations, glue areas, and all critical dimensions needed to assemble the final package.

Check dieline compatibility. THREE-STEP PROCESS:

IF THE USER UPLOADED A DIELINE IMAGE (HTTP flow only):
  POST the image to /upload-image → get image_id → pass here.
  The server uses CLIP to auto-select the closest reference. Skip manual Step 0.

STEP 0 — GET REFERENCES: Call with pack_size ONLY (no dimensions).
  Returns labeled reference dielines filtered by pack size. Each reference has
  BLUE LABELS showing the NAME of each panel (Length, Width, Height, Minor Flap).

STEP 1 — EXTRACT & VERIFY: Call WITH dimensions (no confirmed flag).
  The server shows extracted dimensions for user review.

STEP 2 — CONFIRM: Call WITH confirmed=true after user approves.
  Runs the full compatibility analysis.

🚨 ALWAYS call step 0 FIRST. Do NOT extract dimensions before seeing references.

Required for steps 1-2: case_length, case_width, case_height, pack_size

PRODUCT IDENTIFICATION (do this FIRST, before extracting dimensions):
1. Read the TITLE BLOCK on the dieline — it explicitly states what the product is
   Examples: "12pk 12oz Sleek", "24pk 12oz Standard RSC", "6pk 16oz Std Carton"
   Extract: pack_size, can_size, package_type (carton vs RSC vs tray)
2. Read the BOARD SPEC — identifies carton vs corrugate:
   - Cartons: paperboard thickness 0.018"-0.024" (e.g., "024 CRB", "021 SBS")
   - RSC/Corrugate: flute + ECT (e.g., "B-32ECT", "C-23ECT")
   - Trays: usually corrugate, open-top
3. Check for "Loading Dimensions (W×D×H)" in the spec block — if present, these ARE your dimensions:
   W = case_width, D = case_length (depth), H = case_height

EXTRACTION PROCEDURE (AFTER viewing step 0 references):
<step1> MATCH: Find the reference image whose flat layout matches the user's dieline.
<step2> MAP: The reference's blue labels tell you which panel is Length, Width, Height, etc.
        Find the SAME panels (by position/structure) in the user's dieline.
<step3> READ: Read the NUMBER from each mapped panel in the user's dieline.
        Use exact fractions. Report each number with the dimension NAME from the reference.
        ⚠️ Do NOT derive dimensions arithmetically. READ them from the labeled panels.
<step4> VALIDATE case_height: Must be CLOSE to a known can height (within ~0.25"):
        7.5oz Sleek: 4.088"    8oz Sleek: 4.313"    200ml: 4.310"
        12oz Std: 4.812"       8.4oz Slim: 5.276"    12oz Sleek: 6.127"
        16oz Std: 6.190"       16oz Sleek: 6.807"    19.2oz Std: 7.410"
        24oz Std: 7.610"
        If no match → you mapped the wrong panel as Height → re-check against reference.
<step5> VALIDATE case_width/case_length using pack arrangement and can diameter:
        Can diameters: Sleek=2.259", Std=2.600", Slim=2.080", 24oz=2.862"
        For 12pk (3×4) 12oz Std: width ≈ 3×2.6=7.8", length ≈ 4×2.6=10.4"
        If your values differ by more than 1" from expected, re-check panel mapping.
<step6> IDENTIFY FLAPS: Minor flap = between major flaps in TOP/BOTTOM rows (1.0-2.5").
        The ~1.2" glue flap on left/right edge is NOT minor_flap.

MEASUREMENT PRECISION:
  - Paperboard cartons: measured to 1/64"
  - Corrugate: measured to 1/32"
  Always use EXACT fraction conversions. Common values:
  1 9/32"  = 1.28125  (NOT 1.281)     1 5/32"  = 1.15625  (NOT 1.156)
  4 17/32" = 4.53125  (NOT 4.531)     5 31/32" = 5.96875  (NOT 5.969)

CONFIDENCE SELF-ASSESSMENT (report in extraction_notes):
- HIGH: case_height within 0.25" of known can height AND reference images viewed in step 0
- MEDIUM: Dimensions readable but references NOT viewed — max confidence without step 0
- LOW: Had to guess between two panels, or image resolution insufficient

tools.name: analyze_pallet_pattern
tools.description:
Check pallet pattern compatibility against SOJO's commissioned patterns.

THREE-STEP PROCESS (mirrors dieline analysis):

STEP 0 — GET REFERENCES: Call with pack_config ONLY (and optionally can_size, shipper_type).
  Returns all commissioned patterns grouped by palletizer (DMM, Vention Cobot,
  Vention Industrial, Top Tier) with shipper dims, cases/layer, layers, efficiency.
  Also returns CLIP visual reference images.

STEP 1 — EXTRACT & VERIFY: Call WITH shipper dimensions (shipper_length, shipper_width,
  shipper_height), no confirmed flag.
  Cross-validates your dimensions against known standards for that configuration.
  Shows specs for user review. Flags anomalies (e.g., dims differ from typical).

STEP 2 — CONFIRM: Call WITH confirmed=true after user approves.
  Runs full compatibility analysis against all palletizers:
  - Dimensional constraints (min/max, bump turn limits, pick length)
  - Gripper compatibility (shipper_type → gripper selection)
  - DMM: exact commissioned pattern match required
  - Top Tier: package width, slip sheet availability
  Returns compatibility matrix + matching standard patterns + recommendations.

WHEN A USER UPLOADS A TOPS PRO PDF OR PALLET PATTERN IMAGE:
1. (HTTP flow) POST image to /upload-image → get image_id → pass here for CLIP matching
2. Extract specs from the data table:
   - pack_config: e.g. "24pk", "2x12pk", "4x6pk"
   - can_size: e.g. "12oz Sleek", "12oz Standard", "16oz Standard"
   - shipper_type: "carton", "rsc", or "tray"
   - shipper_length, shipper_width, shipper_height (OD inches from TOPS Pro)
   - cases_per_layer, layers_per_load
   - shipper_pattern: e.g. "4x6x1"
   - pallet_pattern: e.g. "Custom", "Interlock", "Column"
3. Call Step 1 with all extracted params for review
4. Call Step 2 with confirmed=true for full analysis
